draft.title: Stress, anxiety and phobia compared
card: Stress
a response to a stressor, which is something that puts demands on a person. It usually passes once the stressor is gone or has been dealt with.
Anxiety
worry and tension that continues after the stressor has gone, or that occurs without any clear stressor.
Phobia
an intense, irrational fear of a specific object, animal or situation, such as spiders or heights. The fear is far greater than the real danger.
To tell them apart, ask two questions. Is there a stressor, and does the reaction pass? Is the fear tied to one specific thing?
draft.remember: Stress passes with the stressor. Anxiety lingers or has no clear cause. A phobia is fear of one specific thing.

a.q: Which description best fits stress rather than anxiety?
opts: Tension about a exam that eases once the exam is over
Constant worry that has no clear cause
Tension that carries on weeks after a problem is solved
An intense fear of a single object that is not dangerous
a.why: Stress is a response to a stressor and passes when the stressor ends. Constant worry without a cause or after the stressor has gone is anxiety. Intense fear of one harmless object is a phobia.
a.clue: Which reaction eases when the demand is gone?

b.q: Leila feels no worry about heights in daily life, but she freezes and panics on any balcony, even a safe one with a high rail. Which term fits best?
opts: A phobia, as the fear is intense and tied to one thing
Stress, as balconies put demands on her
Anxiety, as the fear is not caused by a stressor
Stress, as the panic ends once she leaves the balcony
b.why: Her fear is intense, out of proportion to the real danger and linked to one specific situation, which is a phobia. Anxiety is not the best fit because her worry is not general. Her panic ending when she leaves does not make it stress, as there is no demand on her.
b.clue: Is the fear general, or aimed at one specific thing?

a.best: Tension about a exam that eases once the exam is over

b.best: A phobia, as the fear is intense and tied to one thing

problems.detail: Grammar error: 'a exam' should be 'an exam'.

The stem says Leila 'feels no worry about heights in daily life' but then panics on balconies, which are heights. This is confusing and could make students doubt that the phobia is of heights. Say instead that she is calm in everyday life away from heights.

Why (b) says 'there is no demand on her', but the card defines a stressor as something that puts demands on a person. A feared balcony can still act as a perceived stressor. A better reason against 'stress' is that her fear is far greater than the real danger and tied to one specific situation.
The remember line says 'Stress passes with the stressor' as a flat rule, but the card says stress 'usually' passes. This drops the card's qualifier.

b.q: Leila is calm in everyday life away from heights. On any balcony, even a safe one with a high rail, she freezes and panics. The panic fades soon after she steps back inside. Which term fits best?
opts: A phobia, as the fear is intense and tied to one thing
Stress, as the panic ends once she leaves the balcony
Anxiety, as the fear has no clear cause
Anxiety, as the worry continues long after she leaves
b.why: Her fear is intense, far greater than the real danger of a safe balcony, and tied to one specific situation, which makes it a phobia. Her panic fading when she leaves is tempting as a sign of stress, but it does not explain fear so out of proportion to a specific, safe situation. It is not anxiety, as the fear has a clear cause and does not linger.
b.clue: Is the fear in proportion to the danger, and aimed at one thing?
